$comment: D-CSUBSET-BITINT-DATA-GLOBAL (registry row opened 2026-07-11 by C1, closed here): a C23 `_BitInt(N)` object with STATIC STORAGE DURATION. Before this example DSS refused every initialized `_BitInt` global — the scalar arm of lowerMirGlobalsToDataItems carried an explicit deferral wall keyed on the BitIntValue pool arm, and a `_BitInt` struct MEMBER refused at the aggregate-leaf recursion, whose sole scalar encoder returns a std::uint64_t and structurally cannot carry an N>64 image. Only a TENTATIVE `_BitInt(17) g;` worked (it reserves .bss through the layout engine and never encodes bytes). clang 18.1.3 and clang 19 `-std=c23` compile and run every declaration here; gcc 13.3.0 `-std=c2x` has no `_BitInt` at all and rejects the declaration itself, so this is required by the clang half of the reference union. ★★ THE PADDING BITS ARE A DECISION AND `g_neg`/`g_s.a` ARE ITS EXECUTABLE FORM: C23 6.2.6.1p6 leaves padding-bit values unspecified; clang zero-fills a static image (MEASURED: `_BitInt(17) = -3wb` emits `fd ff 01 00`) while DSS SIGN-EXTENDS, because that is the invariant its own bitIntMask/maskTopLimb runtime wrap chokepoint establishes (MEASURED by execution: a runtime `_BitInt(17) = -3` reads byte 2 == 0xff, a runtime `_BitInt(65) = -1` reads byte 8 == 0xff). The static image must agree with the runtime that READS it — under a zero-filling emitter `g_neg < 0` is FALSE, because the container would hold +131069. Covers every shape one gate refused: narrow signed negative scalar (.data), narrow unsigned 1-byte scalar, const scalar (.rodata), tentative zero-init (.bss), a 2-limb `_BitInt(128)`, a 4-limb `_BitInt(200)` whose N%64==8 makes the top-limb mask and the 32-byte image length load-bearing, a STRUCT with two `_BitInt` members, an ARRAY of 16-byte `_BitInt(65)` elements (the element stride), a UNION whose first member is `_BitInt(100)`, and `_BitInt` BIT-FIELDS in a static initializer — the aggregate encoder's OTHER leaf, which packs into an allocation unit instead of writing an image, and which MEASURABLY refused before P42 with the generic aggregate text because `decodeScalarLiteralBits` has no BitIntValue arm at all (the RUNTIME twin, examples/c/c23_bitint_bitfield, has always worked, so only the static initializer was walled and nothing named it). The exit is the raw sum of every term the image must carry minus one constant — 3+200+5+7+69+42+5+3+11+200+1+23+29+1+19+13+3+26 = 660, 660-618 = 42 — every term strictly positive, so a global emitted as zero or short moves the exit and no term's loss cancels. ✔MEASURED DISCRIMINATION, by compiling perturbed copies: raising g_w128's HIGH limb 69->70 moves the exit to 43 (value bits above bit 64 are load-bearing); flipping g_neg's sign gives 39; changing the array's SECOND element gives 43; dropping g_w200's top limb gives 37; changing the struct's 1-byte member gives 41. FIVE terms read VALUE BITS ABOVE BIT 64 (g_w128>>64, g_w200>>192, g_w200>>128, g_arr[i]>>64, g_un.w>>99): a low-limb-only emitter reads 0 for all five. A byte-order error inside a limb moves the &255 terms; a limb-order error swaps the >>-terms with them; a 4-byte write into g_u8's 1-byte item overruns it and fails LOUD. g_arr[idx] indexes with argc (an OS-supplied runtime value) so the array bytes must really be in the image and survive the shipped release pipeline. All widths are data-model-independent, so the one exit code holds on all four targets. arm64 runs under qemu; macho on the macos-latest leg.
